title: What Retirement Budgeting Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of retirement budgeting: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Retirement budgeting: estimate spending (often 70-80% of pre-retirement income), map income sources (Social Security, pensions, savings), and plan withdrawals (the 4% guideline).

Why it matters: Many retirees spend 70-80% of pre-retirement income 4% rule: withdraw ~4% of savings yearly (guideline, not law)

This guide walks the full ladder — foundations first, then compounded practice, then advanced mastery. Every record is actionable: read in order, do the steps, run the numbers.

Many retirees spend 70-80% of pre-retirement income
4% rule: withdraw ~4% of savings yearly (guideline, not law)
Healthcare is the wild card - budget generously
Delaying Social Security to 70 boosts benefits ~77% vs 62

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Retirement Budgeting
summary: Start retirement budgeting this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Track current spending for 3-6 months
2. Project retirement spending (housing? travel? health?)
3. List income: Social Security, pensions, rentals
4. Calculate the gap savings must fill
5. Stress-test with a planner or calculator

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.

Project retirement spending (housing? travel? health?)
List income: Social Security, pensions, rentals
Calculate the gap savings must fill
Stress-test with a planner or calculator

title: Common Retirement Budgeting Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
summary: The mistakes everyone makes with retirement budgeting — and the fixes.
body:
The classic errors:

- Ignoring healthcare costs → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- No inflation planning → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Claiming Social Security early by default → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Keeping everything in cash (inflation erodes) → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.

Every mistake above is cheap to prevent and expensive to repair. Prevention is the whole game.

title: Retirement Budgeting Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common retirement budgeting questions.
body:
Q: How much do I need?
A: Roughly 25x annual spending (the 4% rule inverse).

Q: When to claim Social Security?
A: Later = bigger checks; 70 maximizes monthly.

Q: What about inflation?
A: Keep growth assets; don't go all-cash.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.
